business.title: Exergy and environmental sustainability assessment of PV integrated greenhouse cucumber production
business.description: This study examines the thermodynamic and environmental performance of cucumber produced under greenhouse conditions in Türkiye with a holistic approach. The analysis, conducted in the provinces of Kırklareli and Konya, calculated cumulative energy consumption (CEnC), cumulative exergy consumption (CExC), and cumulative CO2 emissions (CCO2E), with a functional unit of one ton of product. In addition, two important sustainability indicators, namely Cumulative Degree of Perfection (CDP) and Renewability Indicator (RI), were calculated based on exergy calculations. According to the results, CEnC was 260.16 MJ/ton, CExC was 1459.82 MJ/ton, and CCO2E was 31.13 kg/ton in Kırklareli, while these values were determined to be 324.38 MJ/ton, 2521.12 MJ/ton, and 50.91 kg/ton, respectively, in Konya. This difference indicates that irrigation and electricity use increase the energy and exergy intensity in Konya. Exergy based sustainability indicators, CDP and RI values, were calculated as 0.73 and − 0.36 for Kırklareli, and 0.42 and − 1.36 for Konya, respectively. These values reveal the high dependence of current production processes on non-renewable energy sources. When photovoltaic (PV) panels were used to supply electricity, the CDP in Kırklareli increased from 0.73 to 0.77, and the RI improved from − 0.36 to -0.30. In Konya, the CDP value rose to 0.51, and the RI to -0.96. These results suggest that PV integration has the potential to improve renewability indicators, especially in energy intensive regions. The findings indicate that, within the scope of this analysis, the sustainability of greenhouse cucumber production could be enhanced through optimized resource management and PV systems.

science.title: Sustainable adsorptive removal of As (III) using Garcinia xanthochymus leaf extract mediated Fe2O3 nanoparticles, regeneration and real water assessment
science.description: Garcinia xanthochymus leaf extract mediated Fe2O3 nanoparticles (GX-Fe2O3 NPs) were successfully synthesized for As (III) adsorption. The pore volume and surface area were found to be 0.2923 cm3/g and 125.7 m2/g respectively, as revealed by BET analysis. The crystallinity of the sample was proven by XRD, with an average crystallite size of 25.47 nm. The measured lattice parameters were a = 5.03 Å and c = 13.93 Å. FTIR confirmed the occurrence of surface functional groups, while FESEM images showed a porous morphology. EDS and XPS confirmed the elemental composition and the adsorption of As (III), evidenced by characteristic binding energy at 44.63 eV, respectively. Batch adsorption studies revealed the optimized parameters as pH:10, dose: 0.5 g/L, initial concentration: 4 mg/L, and temperature: 30 ℃, achieving 71.9% removal efficiency at an equilibrium time of 180 min. The adsorption kinetics followed a PSO model, and the Freundlich isotherm was the best fit, representing multilayer adsorption occurring on a heterogeneous surface. Using the Langmuir isotherm model, the qm was found to be 11.12 mg/g, while the thermodynamic studies confirmed the spontaneity and endothermic nature of the adsorption process. Regeneration studies showed good reusability over five cycles, and the adsorbent was tested across different water matrices. Therefore, the GX-Fe2O3 NPs demonstrate high efficiency and sustainability as a green adsorbent for As (III) uptake.

science.title: A virtual trial framework for generating clinical evidence in orthopedics demonstrated with humeral stem evaluation
science.description: Conventional clinical and experimental approaches cannot systematically evaluate orthopedic implant fixation across the full breadth of patient anatomy, bone quality, and surgical variability. Yet, digital technologies can generate clinically actionable evidence and offer a path to complement conventional preclinical and clinical evaluation of medical devices. Here, we present a virtual trial framework that integrates validated finite-element biomechanical models with machine-learning analytics to quantify implant fixation performance across realistic surgical and anatomical variability. The physics‑based finite‑element models capture bone-implant interactions under physiological loading and have been thoroughly validated against benchtop and clinical data, generating inputs for a machine‑learning layer that identifies key factors influencing primary stability and bone‑remodeling risk. We demonstrate the framework through a case‑study comparison of two humeral stem designs across more than 500 virtual surgeries, sampling patient-specific bone quality, morphology, and surgical alignment. The virtual trial reconstructs clinically relevant patterns of micromotion and stress shielding, revealing how bone density, stem sizing, and alignment jointly influence fixation outcomes. Such relationships are difficult to quantify experimentally or clinically. This digital approach establishes a scalable tool for generation of clinical evidence in orthopedics, with applications in design optimization, preoperative planning, and regulatory decision support.
